text:
maria: Heads-up: saw span attr inconsistency across Python and Go exporters in canary. service.name sometimes missing.
ashok: ugh. is that init race or resource attr override?
maria: looks like our private deploy init path sets resource via env, but Go SDK init path replaced it when we call InitGlobalTracer from runtime.
vik: Could be the SDK merging semantics. Go SDK treats Resource.Create(...) as overriding by default if not merged.
ryan: @maria can you paste logs?
maria: paste: 
```
2026-03-18T09:12:01Z INFO initializing telemetry: resource={}
2026-03-18T09:12:01Z DEBUG otel: exported span service.name=""
```
ashok: That debug line is the exporter, not the SDK. exporter is emitting empty service.name which suggests resource lost earlier.
sara: Is this related to the init shim we added to support VPC/no-egress? It defers exporter creation until network warm-up.
maria: Yes. sequence: init tracer (no exporter), set resource from env, later create exporter and Bsp, register. but when exporter serializes resource it uses default if Resource was nil on creation.
vik: Solution: when creating exporter, pass the merged resource explicitly instead of relying on global state. All langs need the same pattern.
ashok: Also need tests for sampling decision propagation across goroutines. We saw some traces where child goroutine lost parent sampling flag and created full-span payloads. cost hit.
ryan: For Go we use context propagation for sampling. Are we spawning goroutines without context?
sara: yes in kvcache flush path we spawn detached goroutines for async write.
maria: Proposed changes:
- always construct exporter with current Resource attributes (service.name, deployment.env, account_id)
- switch to BatchSpanProcessor with max_queue_size tuned and exporter timeout 10s
- ensure any spawned goroutine that touches spans passes ctx from parent
- add CI smoke that asserts no empty service.name on exported spans
ashok: Agree. Also add graceful-shutdown drain test. We still drop thousands of spans on restart because exporter shutdown timeout too small.
vik: For Rust runtime, Batch processor semantics differ (we use async channel). Increase channel capacity and ensure backpressure when exporter blocks; otherwise we allocate memory per-request.
ryan: Quick note: in Python we saw SimpleSpanProcessor used in a few places. That sends synchronously and blocks request threads. Not ideal for high-throughput inference.
sara: Can we standardize on a small matrix per-lang: default = BSP, fallback = SSP for low-memory envs, and a dialect for private on-prem where egress is blocked (buffer+upload cron)?
maria: Yes. Need an env flag REDWOOD_OTEL_MODE = [default, lowmem, offline] and runtime picks processor/exporter accordingly.
ashok: For offline mode, exporter should write compressed ndjson batch files to local path with rotation and integrity check. CI needs to validate replay consumer reads them with same attribute schema.
ryan: Any opinions on sampling? We should preserve downstream sampling decision (user-set sampler) and ensure SDK respects remote/parent flag. Also add telemetry attrs: rollout_id, model_variant.
vik: Important: avoid adding rollout_id to high-cardinality keys that blow up attribute limits. Use resource attr rollout_id and leave span attrs lean.
sara: On the topic of retention and export: let's add a header in OTLP payload with origin=redwood-sandbox for canaries so we can route to different retention pipelines.
maria: Implementation checklist:
1) fix exporter construction to accept explicit Resource merge (Python/Go/Rust)
2) enforce ctx propagation in kvcache and streaming workers
3) update processors per env modes and doc in internal telemetry guide
4) add CI smoke that exports 50 spans from single request path and asserts resource attrs and sampling flag preserved
5) add shutdown drain test (wait up to 30s, log dropped count)
6) offline exporter writer + replay consumer test
ashok: I'll take Go and coord with infra for egress flag testing.
vik: I'll do Rust changes and add channel capacity tests.
ryan: I'll update Python quickstart and add the CI smoke.
sara: I'll add docs to telemetry-runbook and a checklist for Private deployments.
ci-bot: buildkite: #telemetry-smoke started (pipeline=telemetry-smoke, commit=7a2f1c)
maria: thanks team. will open PRs for Go+Py today.
ryan: thx. tag me on the PRs, I'll review exporter tests. :thumbsup:
